steps: Support airway and ventilation (bag-mask) — hypoxia kills, not the drug per se.
NALOXONE titrated to adequate respiration (not full arousal) — start low to avoid acute withdrawal.
Repeat naloxone or start an infusion (long-acting opioids outlast a naloxone bolus — re-sedation risk).
Observe for a prolonged period after the last naloxone dose; monitor for pulmonary oedema.
Address the cause; harm reduction, take-home naloxone, addiction referral.

drugRefs.freq: repeat every 2–3 min, titrated to adequate respiration
drugRefs.why: Competitive opioid antagonist reversing respiratory depression. Titrate to respiration, not full arousal, to avoid precipitating acute withdrawal. Fentanyl/analogues may need severalfold higher doses.

Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Poisoning and Drug Overdose (Ch.470)

drugRefs.dose: ~two-thirds of the effective waking bolus per hour, titrated
drugRefs.duration: until the opioid effect has worn off; observe after stopping
drugRefs.why: Naloxone lasts only 30–90 min while methadone and sustained-release opioids last far longer, so a bolus alone risks re-sedation. Continue with prolonged observation after discontinuation.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Poisoning and Drug Overdose (Ch.470)

confirm: Reduced consciousness, respiratory depression and PINPOINT pupils; response to naloxone is both diagnostic and therapeutic.
